title: NoAppAccess
wrapsNative: VStack with MonarchEmptyState (lock symbol, Request access and Contact an admin actions, openURL for the mailto: link) and MonarchWorkspaceSwitcher under it
summary: A recipe, not a component: the screen shown in place of an app the signed-in person has no access to, with Request access, Contact an admin and a workspace switcher.
whenToUse: When someone opens an app, or a deep link into one, that their workspace has not given them access to.
whenNotToUse: For a screen that is empty because there is no content yet, use MonarchEmptyState alone. For a missing permission on one action inside an app, disable the action and explain it in place.
api: MonarchEmptyState("You don’t have access to Tickets", message:, systemImage: "lock", actionTitle: isRequested ? nil : "Request access", secondaryActionTitle: "Contact an admin", action:, secondaryAction:)
@Environment(\.openURL) to open the admins' contact link

states.name: no access
states.description: The lock symbol, the title naming the app, the explanation naming the workspace, Request access and Contact an admin.

states.name: requested
states.description: Request access is removed and the message says the request was sent; the app keeps this state while its request is open.

states.name: switching
states.description: The workspace switcher lets the person move to a workspace where they have access.

appearance: MonarchEmptyState's centred layout with the muted symbol, heading and body text and its primary and secondary MonarchButtons, then the workspace switcher's button. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web NoAppAccess is a component with a request state machine, links rendered through the shell's link component, a full-screen mode and heading focus on mount. On iOS it is a recipe: the app's navigation shows this view in place of the app's root, the request is the app's own call, links open with openURL, and VoiceOver focus moves to a new screen by itself. Back to workspace is the system back button or the app's tab bar rather than a link. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: MonarchEmptyState's title has the header trait and the lock symbol is decorative.
Request access and Contact an admin are separate buttons of at least 44 points.
Announce that the request was sent with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement, since the button goes away and focus does not move by itself.
The workspace switcher is a button labelled with the current workspace.
edgeCases: If the request fails, keep Request access and show the failure with MonarchInlineErrorRetry under the empty state.
Without a workspace name, say "Ask a workspace admin" instead of naming the workspace.
Long app and workspace names wrap; the empty state is centred and scrolls inside the app's ScrollView.
